questions.question:
Which of the following factors increases the rate of evaporation?

I. An increase in surface area

II. A decrease in humidity
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****__Both I and II__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The rate of evaporation increases with an increase in surface area.
 
• This is because the evaporation occurs in the molecules that are at the surface, and not the interior.
 
• An increase in humidity would actually decrease the rate of evaporation while vice-versa would increase the rate of evaporation.
 
• Similarly, an increase in wind speed and temperature would increase the rate of evaporation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Evaporation

 
 
• The process of vapourisation which takes place only from the exposed surface of the liquid and at all temperatures is called evaporation.
 
• Evaporation causes cooling.
 
 
 
• Vaporisation
 
 
• The process by which a substance is changed from a liquid state to a vapour state is called vaporisation.

questions.question: The process of conversion of sugar into alcohol is known as ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fermentation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of conversion of **sugar into alcohol** is known as **fermentation.**
 
• Fermentation is a **metabolic process** that converts** sugar to acids, gases, or alcohol.**
 
• The fermentation process is used in food production, such as **bread, cheese, yogurt, and beer.**
 
• In the alcohol industry, fermentation is the first step in the production of **alcoholic beverages.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Denudation** is the process of erosion or stripping away of the earth's surface by natural agents like **water, wind, or ice.**
 
• **Fragmentation** is the breaking up of a larger entity into **smaller pieces.**
 
• **Infiltration** is the movement of water through the** soil surface into the ground.**

questions.question: Helium gas can be converted to the liquid form by the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London forces of attraction**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Helium gas can be liquefied due to the presence of weak intermolecular forces known as **London dispersion forces**.
 
• These forces arise from the momentary distribution of electrons in an atom, leading to a temporary dipole.
 
• London forces are the only intermolecular forces that act between helium atoms, which are non-polar.
 
• Despite being weak, these forces are sufficient to hold helium atoms together in the liquid state at very low temperatures.
 
• **Heike Kamerlingh Onnes** was the first to liquefy helium in 1908 by cooling it to below its boiling point of 4.2 K.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Intermolecular Forces**

 
 
• These are forces of attraction or repulsion between neighboring particles (atoms, molecules, or ions).
 
• Types include London dispersion forces, dipole-dipole interactions, and hydrogen bonding.
 
• London dispersion forces are the weakest, while hydrogen bonds are the strongest among them.
 
 
 
• **Helium**
 
 
• Helium is a noble gas with the atomic number 2 and is the second lightest and second most abundant element in the observable universe.
 
• It is colorless, odorless, tasteless, non-toxic, and inert, making it extremely stable.
 
 
 
• **Liquefaction of Gases**
 
 
• This process involves cooling a gas to a temperature below its critical point, where it can condense into a liquid.
 
• It is used in various industrial processes, including the production of liquefied natural gas (LNG).
 
 
 
• **Critical Temperature**
 
 
• The highest temperature at which a substance can exist as a liquid is called its critical temperature.
 
• For helium, this temperature is extremely low, making its liquefaction a significant scientific achievement.

questions.question: Which gas is released when you combine vinegar and baking soda in a balloon, causing it to inflate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When vinegar (acetic acid) reacts with baking soda (sodium bicarbonate), it produces carbon dioxide gas.
 
• This reaction is an example of an acid-base reaction, which results in the formation of a gas, water, and a salt (sodium acetate).
 
• The carbon dioxide gas produced in the reaction gets trapped in the balloon, causing it to inflate.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: CH₃COOH + NaHCO₃ → CO₂ + H₂O + CH₃COONa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinegar**:

 
 
• Vinegar is a dilute solution of acetic acid (CH₃COOH) in water.
 
• It is commonly used in cooking, cleaning, and as a preservative.
 
 
 
• **Baking Soda**:
 
 
• Baking soda, or sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), is a weak base.
 
• It is used in baking as a leavening agent, in cleaning, and for medical purposes.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂)**:
 
 
• Carbon dioxide is a colorless, odorless gas that is naturally present in the Earth's atmosphere.
 
• It is produced by the respiration of animals and the combustion of fossil fuels.
 
• CO₂ is also used in carbonated beverages and as a refrigerant.
 
 
 
• **Acid-Base Reactions**:
 
 
• These reactions involve the reaction of an acid with a base to produce a salt and water.
 
• Acid-base reactions are fundamental chemical reactions with wide applications in chemistry and industry.

questions.question: Which of the following raw materials is NOT used to prepare the baking soda?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Na₂CO₃**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Baking soda, chemically known as **sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)**, is prepared using sodium chloride (NaCl) as a primary raw material.
 
• The **Solvay process** is the most common method for manufacturing baking soda, which involves the reaction of NaCl, NH₃ (ammonia), and CO₂ in water (H₂O).
 
• **Na₂CO₃ (sodium carbonate)**, also known as washing soda, is not directly used in the preparation of baking soda.
 
• Instead, sodium bicarbonate is derived as an intermediate product in the Solvay process, and Na₂CO₃ is formed as the final byproduct, not as a starting raw material.
 
• Therefore, **Na₂CO₃** is not a raw material used in the manufacturing of baking soda.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Solvay Process:**

 
 
• The Solvay process is an industrial method used to produce sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃) and sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃).
 
• It involves the reaction of sodium chloride (NaCl), ammonia (NH₃), and carbon dioxide (CO₂) in water.
 
• The intermediate product, sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), is filtered out and heated to produce Na₂CO₃.
 
 
 
• **Baking Soda (NaHCO₃):**
 
 
• Baking soda is a white crystalline compound used as a leavening agent in baking.
 
• It releases carbon dioxide (CO₂) gas when it reacts with acids or heats, causing baked goods to rise.
 
• It is also widely used for cleaning, deodorizing, and pH regulation in various applications.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Carbonate (Na₂CO₃):**
 
 
• Also known as washing soda, it is primarily used in laundry detergents, water softening, and glass manufacturing.
 
• It is not a direct component in the preparation of baking soda but is a final byproduct in the Solvay process.
 
 
 
• **Ammonia (NH₃):**
 
 
• Ammonia is a key raw material in the Solvay process, playing a crucial role in precipitating sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃).
 
• It is recovered and reused in the process to minimize waste and reduce costs.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide (CO₂):**
 
 
• CO₂ is another essential raw material in the Solvay process, reacting with ammonia and sodium chloride to form sodium bicarbonate.
 
• It ensures the chemical reaction necessary for the production of baking soda.

questions.question: Ortho-sulphobenzimide is one of the artificial sweeteners. It is also known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Saccharin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saccharin, also known as Ortho-sulphobenzimide, is one of the oldest artificial sweeteners and a popular sugar substitute.
 
• It is approximately 300–400 times sweeter than sucrose (table sugar), requiring only a small amount to achieve desired sweetness.
 
• Saccharin is calorie-free, making it suitable for people managing weight or controlling diabetes.
 
• It is widely used in products such as diet beverages, baked goods, toothpaste, and pharmaceutical formulations due to its stability under heat and storage.
 
• Saccharin was discovered in 1879 by Constantin Fahlberg and became commercially available in the early 20th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Artificial Sweeteners:**

 
 
• Artificial sweeteners are chemical compounds that mimic the sweetness of sugar while providing fewer or no calories.
 
• Examples include saccharin, aspartame, sucralose, and alitame, which are widely used in food and beverages.
 
• They are commonly used to aid in calorie reduction and diabetes management.
 
 
 
• **Aspartame:**
 
 
• Aspartame is an artificial sweetener that is about 200 times sweeter than sucrose.
 
• It is commonly found in diet sodas, sugar-free gum, and other low-calorie products.
 
• Unlike saccharin, aspartame provides calories but is used in very small amounts, making its caloric contribution negligible.
 
 
 
• **Sucralose:**
 
 
• Sucralose is a chlorinated derivative of sucrose and is about 600 times sweeter than regular sugar.
 
• It is heat-stable and is commonly used in baking and cooking.
 
• Sucralose is marketed under the brand name Splenda.
 
 
 
• **Health Considerations:**
 
 
• Artificial sweeteners like saccharin are approved by regulatory authorities for safe consumption.
 
• Saccharin was once linked to cancer in laboratory animals, but subsequent studies confirmed its safety for humans within regulated limits.
 
• Regulatory bodies like the FDA and WHO continuously monitor the safety of artificial sweeteners.

questions.question: The process of seepage of water into the land is called _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** infiltration.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Infiltration**

 
 
• **​**The **process of seepage of water into the land** is called infiltration.
 
• Water not used by plants moves deeper into the ground. 
 
• Infiltration rate in soil science is a measure of the rate at which soil is able to absorb rainfall or irrigation.
 
• The rate of infiltration can be measured using an **infiltrometer.**
 
• The main factors that influence the infiltration are:
 
 
• **the soil type**
 
• **the soil coverage**
 
• **the topography and morphology of slopes**
 
• **the flow supply**
 
• **the initial condition of soil humidity**
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Depletion**

 
 
• Depletion is the** reduction in the quantity of a factor of production **as a result of the production process.
 
• Companies use existing goods and services to create new goods and services.
 
• The conversion of existing goods into new goods is known as a production process.
 
• There are two types of depletion:
 
 
• **Percentage depletion**
 
• **Cost depletion**

questions.question: What is the atomic number of uranium (U)?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**92**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uranium** is a chemical element with the symbol **U** and atomic number **92**.
 
• It is a **radioactive element** that belongs to the actinide series in the periodic table.
 
• Uranium is used primarily as **fuel in nuclear reactors** and to produce **nuclear weapons**.
 
• It is found naturally in **earth's crust**, primarily as uranium-238 and uranium-235 isotopes.
 
• Uranium-235 is significant because of its ability to undergo **nuclear fission**, which is used in nuclear power generation.
 
• Uranium is mined in various countries, including **Canada, Kazakhstan, and Australia**.
 
• It is processed into **yellowcake**, a concentrated form of uranium oxide, before being used in reactors.
 
• The discovery of Uranium dates back to **1789** by German chemist Martin Heinrich Klaproth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Rutherfordium**:**__

 __
 
• Atomic number **104** corresponds to the element **Rutherfordium**, not Uranium.
 
• Rutherfordium is a **synthetic element** and is part of the transition metals group.
 
• It was first discovered in **1964** by a team of Russian scientists.
 
 
 
• Plutonium**:**__
 __
 
• Atomic number **94** corresponds to the element **Plutonium**.
 
• Plutonium is a **radioactive actinide metal** and is used in **nuclear reactors** and **nuclear weapons**.
 
• It was first isolated in **1940** by scientists at the University of California, Berkeley.
 
 
 
• Thorium**:**__
 
 
• Atomic number **90** corresponds to the element **Thorium**.
 
• Thorium is a **weakly radioactive metal** and is considered a potential alternative to uranium in **nuclear reactors.**
 
• It was discovered in **1828** by Swedish chemist Jöns Jakob Berzelius.

questions.question: Which of the following bases is found in window cleaner?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ammonium hydroxide.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **aqueous solution, ammonium hydroxide,** is created by** saturating water** with **gaseous ammonia.**
 
• The colorless ammonium hydroxide solution is a **weak basic.**
 
• It does not** entirely ionize**, leaving the water molecule.
 
• This solution is employed as a** buffer solution,** or a solution that is used t**o modify the pH in a chemical reaction. ** 
 
• Because the concentration of **OH- ions **in the solution rises, the basicity of the solution also rises.
 
• A strong reagent with the ability to** dissolve stains** brought on by **vegetable fats, animal fats,** etc. is** ammonium hydroxide.**
 
• As a result, the substance is effective as a **cleaning agent and readily vaporizes.**
 
• Thus, it is a component of** detergents** for **cleaning glass, windows, and other surfaces.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Magnesium hydroxide:**

 
 
• Magnesium hydroxide is a **short-term treatmen**t for adults and children who experience **sporadic constipation.**
 
• **Saline laxatives** are a group of drugs that include magnesium hydroxide.
 
• It functions by making the** feces retain water.**
 
 
 
• **Sodium hydroxide:**
 
 
• Sodium hydroxide is a chemical that manufacturers utilize to make things like** soap, rayon, paper, explosives, colors, and petroleum products.**
 
 
 
• **Calcium hydroxide:**
 
 
• **Indirect and direct pulp cupping, root dressing, root canal sealant**, and apical closure are all possible uses for calcium hydroxide.
